extracted.intended_audience: UK research organisations, businesses and researchers seeking UKRI funding
extracted.subtask_description: Browse and determine eligibility and fit for open and upcoming UKRI funding calls. The page lists individual opportunities with funder, eligibility constraints, scope, award ranges, and opening/closing dates to help applicants decide which calls to apply to.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant location / organisation registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant organisations must be UK registered organisations (or UK registered businesses) to apply to certain Innovate UK calls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples from the page: 'UK registered organisations can apply' (Battery Innovation Programme; Dual-use aviation systems and autonomy), 'UK registered businesses can apply' (National Materials Innovation Programme: Feasibility studies). Where calls are Innovate UK–led, applicants are frequently required to be UK-registered entities. Check each opportunity for exact wording and permitted organisation types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant must be based at a UK research organisation eligible for the funder
rubrics_metrics.description: Many opportunities require applicants to be based at a UK research organisation that is eligible to receive funding from a specific research council (EPSRC, BBSRC, NERC, MRC, STFC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verbatim examples: 'You must be based at a UK research organisation eligible for EPSRC funding.'; 'You must be based at a UK research organisation eligible for BBSRC funding.'; 'You must be based at a UK research organisation eligible for NERC funding.'; 'You must be a researcher based at a research organisation eligible to apply for MRC funding.'; 'You must be based at a UK research organisation eligible for Science and Technology Facilities Council (STFC) funding.' Applicants should confirm institutional eligibility with the named funder/council for each opportunity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project scope must align with the programme remit
rubrics_metrics.description: Each funding opportunity specifies the thematic remit or intended outcomes the project must address (for example, battery skills, quantum commercialisation skills, aviation dual‑use technologies, materials translation, particle physics experiment research, environmental global partnerships, experimental medicine, cybersecurity in critical sectors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'to establish or scale regional skills initiatives for battery manufacturing and its supply chain'; 'establish a UK centre for quantum commercialisation skills that will provide opportunities for researchers to develop commercialisation skills, engage with industry, and explore new career pathways'; 'development of aviation technologies and systems that support both civil and military use cases'; 'feasibility studies ... to speed the translation of advanced materials innovations in three prioritised high growth themes and one strategic opportunity theme'; 'support particle physics experiment research'. Applicants must design proposals that clearly map to the stated aims and scope of the specific call.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory inclusion of international project partners (where stated)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some calls require the inclusion of at least one international project partner as a condition of application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit example: 'The inclusion of one or more international project partners is mandatory.' (Environmental sciences: Global Partnerships Seedcorn Fund 2026). Applicants must ensure partner organisations meet any nationality/eligibility rules and document their roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human intervention requirement for clinical/experimental medicine calls
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain biomedical/clinical calls require the proposed work to include an intervention in humans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verbatim example: 'Your application must include an intervention in humans.' (Experimental medicine stage one). For these calls, clinical trial/ethical/regulatory considerations will be central to eligibility and assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community membership or domain-specific eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Some opportunities limit applications to members of a defined research community or domain (beyond institutional eligibility).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'You must be ... a member of the UK particle physics community.' (Particle Physics Experiment Consolidated Grants 2026). Applicants should verify what constitutes membership and provide evidence where required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding type and funding instrument
rubrics_metrics.description: Each opportunity specifies the type of funding instrument (for example, Grant or Contracts for Innovation) and any programme-specific commercialisation/contracting expectations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Displayed labels include 'Funding type: Grant' or specific programme names like 'Contracts for Innovation'. The instrument affects allowable costs, VAT treatment, procurement/contracting terms and expectations (e.g., demonstration/commercialisation requirements versus research grants).

rubrics_metrics.name: Award range, maximum award, and total fund availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Opportunities state available funding levels such as maximum award per project, award ranges, and total programme budgets which constrain how much funding an applicant may request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'Award range: £10,000,000 - £11,300,000' (Centre for Quantum Commercialisation Skills); 'Total fund: £3,700,000' (Battery Innovation Programme); 'Maximum award: £100,000' (Environmental sciences Seedcorn). Applicants must request amounts within the stated ranges and may need to justify budget and match funding if required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project delivery expectations (development, demonstration, commercialisation, real end-user environment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some calls require that projects progress beyond research to demonstration and/or commercialisation in operational environments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'to develop, demonstrate and commercialise their cybersecurity solution in real end user environments within critical sector organisations.' (Contracts for Innovation: Cyber scale in critical sectors). Projects should plan for real-world trials, stakeholder engagement, and routes to market where the call demands it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opening and closing dates / application timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Each opportunity defines precise opening and closing dates and times which determine the application window.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'Opening date: 7 May 2026 9:30am UK time; Closing date: 18 June 2026 11:00am UK time.' Applicants must submit within these windows; late submissions are typically not accepted. Also note some calls show 'Open - no closing date' for rolling calls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity status labelling
rubrics_metrics.description: Opportunities are labelled with statuses such as 'Open' or 'Upcoming' which indicate whether applications are being accepted now or will open later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples on page: 'Opportunity status: Open' and 'Opportunity status: Upcoming'. Use status to plan applications and preparatory work; read opportunity details for the exact opening time/date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target applicant career stage or role (where specified)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some funding routes are tailored to applicants at particular career stages or roles (for example, 'new investigator' awards targeting early-career researchers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'BBSRC new investigator award: applicant-led mode' signals the scheme targets new investigators; full eligibility and expectations should be checked in the scheme guidance for criteria such as independence and track record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programme co-funding or partnership expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain calls list co-funders or international partners and may carry expectations about partnership models or co-funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'Co-funders: São Paulo Research Foundation (FAPESP), National Science and Technology Council (NSTC) Taiwan' (Environmental sciences Seedcorn). Applicants should review the call for any co-funding rules, eligibility differences for partner countries and expected collaboration arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Call-specific deliverables or outputs implied in scope text
rubrics_metrics.description: Some opportunities state required or expected deliverables (e.g., establishing a centre, creating sustainable partnerships, feasibility study outcomes) which proposals must commit to deliver.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'establish a UK centre for quantum commercialisation skills that will provide opportunities for researchers to develop commercialisation skills, engage with industry, and explore new career pathways'; 'Apply for funding to create new and sustainable global partnerships in environmental science'; 'feasibility studies ... to speed the translation of advanced materials innovations'. Applicants should align their workpackages, milestones and KPIs to these expected outputs.
